summary.headline: FY26 bookings hit record INR1,550 crore (+22% YoY) while FY26 revenue fell to INR564 crore from INR713 crore on revenue-recognition timing.
summary.overview: Arvind SmartSpaces reported record FY26 bookings of INR1,550 crore, up 22% YoY, with Q4 bookings crossing INR600 crore for the first time. Full-year revenue declined to INR564 crore from INR713 crore, which management attributed to timing of revenue recognition and occupation certificates slipping into FY27, while adjusted EBITDA fell to INR156 crore and PAT to INR103 crore. Q4 PAT rose 103% YoY to INR44 crore on revenue of INR155 crore. Business development added projects worth INR3,140 crore in FY26, and a further INR2,400 crore Mumbai high-rise was signed after year-end.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR163 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Bengaluru
segments.commentary: Contributed INR485 crore of FY26 bookings, about 31% of total. Arvind Skycrest in Bannerghatta sold 164 units worth INR262 crore (about 53% of inventory) within a week of launch.

segments.name: Vadodara
segments.commentary: Arvind Greenfields on Ajwa Road sold 323 units worth INR178 crore, about 42% of launched inventory, in its launch quarter.

segments.name: Mumbai MMR
segments.commentary: Three projects in portfolio: Santacruz redevelopment, Goregaon MHADA redevelopment (JV with Oxford Sigma, 44% profit share), and Pen-Khopoli plotted project (INR1,500 crore, phase 1 INR500-600 crore). Newly signed high-rise worth about INR2,400 crore after year-end.

segments.name: Ahmedabad
segments.commentary: Vastrapur high-rise added in FY26; first launch expected in H1 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 BD lock-in target of INR4,000-5,000 crore GDV; BD spend expected slightly above FY26's roughly INR600 crore.
FY27 bookings growth guided at 35-40%, with sustenance sales growing about 15%; long-term bookings CAGR 25-30% over 4-5 years.
About 6 launches planned in FY27 (1 Ahmedabad, 3 Bengaluru, 2 Mumbai) with inventory of INR3,000-3,500 crore; H2 launch weighting expected.
Operating cash flow in FY27 expected to be roughly flat versus FY26 in absolute terms as construction spend ramps.
No explicit revenue guidance; management expects strong growth over FY26 reported revenue as delayed occupation certificates move into FY27.
Projects targeted at 22-25% EBITDA margin on new sales; OCF as a share of collections likely 25-30% for next few years.
Net debt-to-equity to stay below 1:1; currently 0.26. Unrealised operating cash flow of over INR4,970 crore expected over 4-5 years.
Final dividend recommended at INR2.25 per share (face value INR10).
capex_capacity: About 6 launches planned in FY27 across Ahmedabad, Bengaluru and Mumbai, with some large launches to be phased.
Pen-Khopoli (Mumbai, plotted) is the most advanced Mumbai launch; Santacruz or Goregaon to follow in FY27.
Forest Trails (Bengaluru row houses/villas) site experience and show villa expected ready in 3-4 months; sales activation to restart in FY27.
HDFC platform of INR600 crore, of which INR350 crore used; the balance is being backfilled as available-on-call lines for any product type.
Three HDFC-linked Bengaluru projects use OCD structures.
demand_pricing: Management says demand has stabilised and become more organised after a euphoric period; Bannerghatta's 50%+ sale was a single weekend, with approvals only in the last 7 days of the quarter.
Sustenance sales exceeded INR600 crore in FY26, with about INR180 crore in Q4.
Commodity and material costs up about 4% pre-war versus post-war; management says contingency budgeting absorbs it and no price pass-through is needed yet.
Surat project dropped due to technical and legal complexities.
Cancellations in Forest Trails: about INR11 crore and 5 units in FY26, which management says are part of regular sustaining-stage business.

qa_highlights.question: What is the equity investment behind FY26 BD and the FY27 BD guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 BD was about INR3,200 crore with investing outflow of about INR600 crore; FY27 BD lock-in target is INR4,000-5,000 crore. Project-wise capital breakup not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the OCF as a percentage of collections stay at 36-37%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects it to converge to the 22-25% EBITDA margin profile over time; for the next few years it could be 25-30%, helped by plotted projects and pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 bookings growth of 35-40% conservative given launch timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch pipeline is weighted to H2, with the Ahmedabad project possibly in H1; approval slippage is a risk, but management is reasonably sure of timelines.

qa_highlights.question: How will the unsold launched inventory of about INR3,000 crore be sold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that about 3 years is a fair assumption for launched inventory, while overall portfolio monetisation is 4-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be held given rising costs from the Middle East crisis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is confident of 22-25% margins on new sales; a short commodity spike of a quarter or so can be absorbed within budgeted contingency.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Goregaon JV structure?
qa_highlights.answer: JV with Oxford Sigma on a MHADA redevelopment; Arvind has a 44% profit share, and the partner handles site management and approvals, with Arvind leading development, sales and construction.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition depends on occupation certificates; FY27 revenue recovery depends on timely approvals.
Launch slippage risk: H2 weighting of six launches could push part of the 35-40% bookings growth into FY28.
Commodity cost inflation (about 4% so far) could pressure margins if it lasts beyond a few quarters.
Forest Trails has over 50% unsold inventory and cancellations in FY26.
Sustenance sales growth guided at about 15% in FY27; a slowdown would weigh on bookings.
Shift to OCF-light, asset-light MMR deals and rising construction spend could lower OCF conversion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, pipeline and margins, with clear caveats on revenue timing and approvals. Management declined to give revenue or debt guidance and deferred several project-level questions offline.
key_quotes: During the year, we achieved our highest ever annual booking value of INR1,550 crores, representing a strong 22% year-on-year growth.
we are fairly confident that we can continue to maintain the trajectory of 22% to 25% even in the current year.
Having said this, in our own budgeting, we have taken a sufficiently large cushion in the form of contingency and inflation that we normally budget as a part of our practice.
We are at 0.26 net debt-to-equity ratio, as you see.
